steps.name: QC + DE (pydeseq2) for aldosterone vs vehicle
caveats: n=6/group, single batch: no batch correction possible or needed; power is limited, so small |log2FC| effects will not be significant - report the expected nulls rather than hiding them.
Length-corrected counts carry a mild bias; if rounding was applied, state it in the results.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-without-tf-activity-python-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples + name column, Salmon gene-level output) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-tf-activity-python-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample + condition). Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, Homo sapiens, kidney. The data profile does not state whether the Salmon matrix is length-corrected, so the count scale must be diagnosed before DESeq2.
steps.question: After QC of all 12 samples, which genes are differentially expressed in the 6 aldosterone-treated samples vs the 6 vehicle-control samples of human kidney?
constraints: Python only: pydeseq2, pandas, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, matplotlib, seaborn. No R in any script (user constraint).
Read condition strings as they appear in metadata.csv; identify the treated group as the aldosterone group and the baseline as the vehicle/control group. Do not assume the label strings a priori.

Count sanity check: if the matrix holds floats (length-scaled Salmon output), round to nearest integers and explicitly report that DE ran on length-corrected counts (tximport-style approximation). If per-sample totals are ~1e4 (TPM-like) rather than ~1e6-1e8, stop with a diagnostic report instead of forcing DESeq2.
QC per sample: total counts, genes detected, pairwise correlation; PCA on log2(1+CPM). Report any outlier, but with 6/group do not drop a sample unless it is provably a duplicate or mislabel.
Filter genes with CPM >= 1 in >= 4 samples; report kept gene count.

DESeq2 via pydeseq2: design ~ condition with vehicle/control as the reference level so log2FC is treated vs control; Wald test; LFC shrinkage (apeglm prior if this pydeseq2 version supports it, else normal prior - record which was used). Run a ~20-gene toy-matrix smoke test of the DeseqObj/lfc_shrinkage API first, because documentation lookup failed during planning (HTTP 429) and signatures must be verified in-sandbox before the real run.
Save all outputs to the step directory with the exact file names: de_results.csv, expr_logcpm.csv, sample_qc.csv, pca.png, ma.png, volcano.png.
steps.description: Produces de_results.csv (all kept genes: baseMean, shrunken log2FC, pvalue, padj), expr_logcpm.csv (kept genes x 12 samples, log2(1+CPM)), sample_qc.csv, and figures pca.png, ma.png, volcano.png.
acceptance_criteria: de_results.csv covers every kept gene with finite shrunken log2FC and padj.
The count scale/integerity diagnostic is reported, including whether rounding was applied and why.
QC metrics and PCA exist for all 12 samples, colored by the actual condition labels.
DE gene counts at FDR<0.1 and FDR<0.05 with up/down direction counts are reported.

steps.name: TF activity: decoupler on CollecTRI + DoRothEA
caveats: Module scores are correlative activity estimates from cell-type-agnostic curated networks; 'drives' is an inference, not a causal claim.
n=6/group: expect few TFs to reach FDR<0.05; report both FDR-significant and nominal-p<0.05 lists and say which is which.
The DoRothEA RDA needs an R runtime via rpy2; verify the import works in-sandbox before the main run, and if rpy2 fails, proceed on CollecTRI alone and flag the missing sensitivity network.
steps.context: Primary data: expr_logcpm.csv and de_results.csv from T1S1 (12 samples, 6 aldosterone vs 6 vehicle). Reference networks, all Homo sapiens (matches dataset), confirmed present in the reference store: a curated signed human TF-target regulon network in CSV (CollecTRI 2.0, columns source/target/weight, /mnt/refs/managed/collectri-human/2.0/CollecTRI_regulons.csv) and curated signed human DoRothEA regulons with per-edge confidence A-E in RDA (/mnt/refs/managed/dorothea-human/current/dorothea_hs.rda, load via rpy2, keep confidence A-C).
steps.question: Which TF modules show different activity in the 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle-control kidney samples, and which TFs' target genes are enriched among the up- vs down-regulated DE genes?
constraints: Python only: decoupler, rpy2, pandas, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, matplotlib, seaborn.

Verify both reference files exist and are the human sets before use; if one is missing, proceed with the other and report the gap - never substitute the mouse networks or the predicted-only GTRD GMT as the primary network.
Build the decoupler network from (source, target, weight); report TF count, target count, and the fraction of network targets present in the expression matrix.

Score TF modules on the 12-sample logCPM expression with decoupler (method 'PLAGEM', 'Umax' if unavailable) for BOTH networks. Run a toy-subset smoke test of the decoupler API first, because documentation lookup failed during planning (HTTP 429); adapt call signatures if needed without changing the statistical design.
Per-TF condition test: Mann-Whitney U between the 6 treated and 6 control module scores (Welch t as sensitivity), BH FDR across TFs via statsmodels multipletests.

Differential-regulation enrichment: rank genes by shrunken log2FC (full signed list); test per-TF enrichment of activating targets among top up-DE genes and repressing targets among top down-DE genes (decoupler.dr if the API is available, otherwise an explicit rank-sum test against network weights).
Report cross-network reproducibility: overlap of the top-50 TF sets between CollecTRI and DoRothEA results.
Save outputs exactly as: tf_activity_collectri.csv, tf_activity_dorothea.csv, tf_dr.csv, top_tfs.png, tf_score_heatmap.png.
steps.description: Produces tf_activity_collectri.csv and tf_activity_dorothea.csv (per TF: per-sample scores or condition means, delta treated-control, p, BH padj, direction), tf_dr.csv (per-TF enrichment of signed targets in the DE ranked list), cross-network reproducibility report, and figures top_tfs.png and tf_score_heatmap.png.
acceptance_criteria: tf_activity_*.csv cover every TF in each network with finite statistics and a BH padj.
Network coverage statistics (TFs, targets, target overlap with measured genes) are reported for both networks.
Cross-network reproducibility of the top TFs is reported.
Figures and all CSVs are saved to the step directory.

steps.name: Pathway context of the DE list
caveats: GO sets are nested - do not present correlated hits as independent findings.
WikiPathways coverage is uneven; report set sizes alongside significance.
steps.context: Input: de_results.csv from T1S1 (full ranked list + FDR<0.05 up/down sets). Reference gene sets, all Homo sapiens, confirmed present: MSigDB human hallmark (50 sets, /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt), MSigDB human GO-BP (7,538 sets, /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-go-human/2026.1/c5.go.bp.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt), human WikiPathways (2026.07.10, /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt).
steps.question: Which human pathways and programs (hallmark, GO biological process, WikiPathways) are enriched among genes up- vs down-regulated by aldosterone treatment?
constraints: Python only: gseapy (prerank), blitzgsea as the fgsea fallback, pandas, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, matplotlib, seaborn. Offline only - no gseapy.enrichr and no network access of any kind.
Prerank GSEA (fgsea) on the full ranked list (signed shrunken log2FC) for each of the three GMT collections; report NES and FDR per set and direction.
Over-representation of the FDR<0.05 up-list and down-list against hallmark and GO-BP (scipy hypergeometric, set size >= 15, BH across sets).
Report symbol-overlap statistics (fraction of ranked-list and DE-list genes present in each GMT) before interpreting any result.
Save outputs exactly as: gsea_prerank_hallmark.csv, gsea_prerank_gobp.csv, gsea_prerank_wikipathways.csv, or_up.csv, or_down.csv, pathway_dotplots.png.
steps.description: Produces gsea_prerank_hallmark.csv, gsea_prerank_gobp.csv, gsea_prerank_wikipathways.csv, or_up.csv, or_down.csv, and dot-plot figures of the top 15 sets per direction.
acceptance_criteria: Prerank tables exist for all three collections plus OR tables for up and down.
Overlap statistics are reported for each GMT.
The interpretation notes GO hierarchy redundancy (nested parent/child sets) rather than counting raw significant hits.

steps.name: Consensus TF ranking + interpretation
caveats: TFs supported by only one evidence stream must be labeled as such; a single-network rank is not a consensus.
Do not claim the TFs bind the mineralocorticoid receptor or directly mediate aldosterone signaling - the inference is network-activity based.
steps.context: Inputs: tf_activity_collectri.csv, tf_activity_dorothea.csv, tf_dr.csv from T2S1; de_results.csv from T1S1; T3S1 pathway tables for interpretive context.
steps.question: Integrating TF module activity from both networks, DR direction, and TF-gene expression, which transcription factors most plausibly drive the aldosterone response in these kidney samples?
constraints: Python only: pandas, numpy, matplotlib, seaborn.

Per-TF consensus table: activity delta and padj for each network, DR direction, the TF's own log2FC and padj where its gene is measured, and a consistency flag for direction agreement across streams. Rank by mean rank across available streams; state the exact formula in the output file metadata.

Sanity-anchor probe (verification, not prediction): report the measured log2FC/padj of canonical aldosterone/kidney MR-response genes SCNN1A, SCNN1B, SCNN1G, NEDD4L, AGTR1, THBS1 from the DE table, and the measured status of NR3C2 (mineralocorticoid receptor) itself; note whether the top TFs are plausible downstream effectors of the MR program.

Write interpretation.md separating observation (activity/enrichment statistics) from interpretation (putative driving mechanism), and state explicitly that inference is network-activity based and correlative.
Save outputs exactly as: consensus_tf_table.csv, top_tfs_consensus.png, interpretation.md.
steps.description: Produces consensus_tf_table.csv (all TFs, all evidence streams, documented rank), top_tfs_consensus.png, and interpretation.md with the top-10 ranked TF list (direction + per-TF evidence + confidence).
acceptance_criteria: Consensus table carries all evidence streams for every TF with the ranking formula documented.
A ranked top-10 TF list exists with direction and a per-TF confidence label.
interpretation.md explicitly separates observation from interpretation and states the correlative-inference limitation.
The sanity-anchor probe results are reported.

plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney RNA-seq: DE and TF drivers
plan.analytical_narrative: Human kidney bulk RNA-seq, 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle-control samples (unpaired, single batch), Salmon gene-level counts, 12,000 genes x 12 samples; record is ambiguous about length correction, so T1S1 diagnoses count scale first. Python-only pipeline per user constraint: T1S1 QC + DESeq2 via pydeseq2 (LFC shrinkage) producing the DE table and a normalized logCPM matrix; T2S1 TF-activity inference by decoupler module scoring against two independent signed human TF-target networks (CollecTRI 2.0 primary; DoRothEA A-C as sensitivity), per-TF condition tests on module scores, and differential-regulation enrichment of the signed DE ranked list; T3S1 pathway/functional context of the DE list (MSigDB human hallmark, GO-BP, human WikiPathways, offline prerank); T3S2 consensus TF ranking integrating activity deltas across both networks, DR direction, and TF-gene expression, with a sanity probe against canonical kidney MR-response genes. n=6/group limits power; the deliverable is an evidence-ranked, direction-labeled TF list with correlative (not causal) inference stated as such.
